precepts.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said. Let us search and try our ways.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. Looked up in class: offscouring is a rare noun that means physical dirt or refuse cleaned off an object, or a person rejected by society as an outcast. Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Paul is talking about the same thing: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: let us search and try our ways.

This is a lot of times what we as a people do not want to do: examine ourselves. What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” You have to prove your own self, whether Christ is in you or not. And that is where turning again to the Lord starts. Jeremiah goes on, “We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned”, and that is why we are in this state, the condition we are in now. A people who will not examine themselves will never see why the Lord has covered himself with a cloud, and will never turn again to him.

precepts.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? If you do not know Christ is in you, you are reprobate. That is what all of us have to do: examine ourselves day by day.
precepts.point: Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways. You know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. And do not say that is only for Zerubbabel; it is not.
precepts.why:
Haggai says, “Now therefore thus saith the Lord of hosts; Consider your ways.” Do you know what consider your ways means? Examine yourself. Paul says it: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?”

If you don't know Christ is in you, you are reprobate. That is what all of us have to do: examine ourselves day by day. And don't say consider your ways was only for Zerubbabel; it is not.

Haggai shows what happens when we don't. “Ye have sown much, and bring in little”: you worked a lot with little profit to show for it. “Ye eat, but ye have not enough ... and he that earneth wages earneth wages to put it into a bag with holes.” I just worked 48, 52 hours, and I don't have enough money to show for it. That was going on with Zerubbabel, and it is why many of us are always struggling: because God is second or third in your life, just like Zerubbabel. “Because of mine house that is waste, and ye run every man unto his own house.”

When Zerubbabel and Joshua heard it, they “obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, and the words of Haggai the prophet”. Haggai was not governor or high priest, but they humbled themselves, because they knew it was the word of the Lord. They did not say, arrest him. That is how we have to be. When we correct a brother he takes it personal, like we stabbed his mama; correct his wife and he says you are trying to destroy my marriage. No, we are trying to help. That's love. Examine yourself and fix your life.

precepts.text: Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.
precepts.point: We had one brother just leave saying Captain Abiel kept putting too much pressure on him. What do you mean pressure? He is forcing me to go out and teach and do God's work, forcing me to be accountable. Spirits like that: just leave. Nobody is going to cry over spilled milk.
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” This is about self-examination, and it goes for all of us. “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”, so what was read about those men in Maccabees pertains to us even today, because there are men and women with those same hateful attributes.

The wise man says the same: “Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.” Examine yourself now, before judgment comes, and you will find mercy when the Lord visits.

What were those men's problems? Not sexual lust; nothing read that day was about a woman. It was covetousness: covetousness of power and authority, men wanting certain seats. From that came hatred, betrayal, a traitor, lies, theft, stealing from the temple, and murder. Everybody's demon is not the same. Covetousness is number ten of the commandments, but it is where all the others start, because it is internal, within you and me. Those are the sins to examine ourselves for.

One brother just left saying Captain Abiel kept putting too much pressure on him. What pressure? He is forcing me to go out and teach and do God's work, forcing me to be accountable. Are you kidding me? A spirit like that that will not examine itself, just leave. Nobody is going to cry over spilled milk. The one who examines himself before judgment finds mercy in the day of visitation.

Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is; we can tell you, brother, you are off, there is sin in there, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves”: not your neighbor, yourself. And you can do it, because “The heart knoweth his own bitterness”. Your mind knows its own bitterness. Brother, sister, you can't play confused when somebody asks, man, where is that bitterness coming from?

“and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.” So you can't say, oh Bishop, tell me what's going on with me. You know exactly what is going on in your mind. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is. We can say, brother, you're off, you ain't moving right, there is sin in there; we may not know it specifically, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife, and then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. If that spirit is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. That is why each of us has to prove our own self: the heart already knows where the bitterness is.

precepts.text: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: and see if there be any wicked way in me. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly. And how does he search you? You have to search the scriptures.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
To examine ourselves we ask the Lord to do it with us: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me”. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly.

How is he going to do that? When you say, Lord, search me, that means you have to search the scriptures. The Lord ain't going to come down and say, open that door right there, let me see what's behind it. No, brother. You have to search the scriptures.

Then, in order to get over the root of bitterness, we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. We look to the scriptures and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit, bitter toward my wife, toward the leadership, toward my brother, and we pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is how we prove our own selves, whether we be in the faith.

precepts.text: Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed.
precepts.point: Knowing yourself means catching the thought and saying, not today, because you know where it leads.
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves”. Every brother and sister must examine themselves, and nobody can prove you but you. Ask yourself what you are doing that keeps you from growing in the spirit of Christ, and what you need help with. Do not wait until you hit rock bottom. The faith is the scriptures, and you must constantly examine yourself to see that you are still in it, because Satan can bind us while we still think we are in the truth, hardly reading, hardly studying, hardly watching class.

Knowing yourself means knowing your triggers and your weak point. If you are covetous, you should not have a job dealing with money. If you are lustful, you should not be watching certain videos or listening to R&B heavy. Music, movies and social media will lead you to porn. My lust and your lust might be different, but if I know myself, I know mine. So when the thought comes you say, self, we ain't going to do that today, turn it off and meditate on the scriptures. If you do not examine yourself, you are reprobate, and you let Satan use your body to do whatever he wants.

Why does it matter so much? “Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed”. Satan wants us to shame the ministry, and he makes us believe it is just a little thing. But people want to prove us wrong. They are ready to pick at any little thing: see what leadership is doing, see what the brothers and sisters are doing. Satan sets people inside the congregations for this, ready to say, I'm offended, I'm leaving.

Yet offences are everywhere. Solomon offended, and the whole of Israel was not destroyed; Israel still went on. One man's sin does not destroy everything, which is why we pray and fast for our leadership to stay on course. So take every little thing as a big thing, keep examining yourself, and do not go back to sin, so that the ministry is not blamed.

precepts.text: The Lord knoweth them that are his. Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity; in a great house are vessels to honour and to dishonour.
precepts.point: Examine yourselves whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves, except ye be reprobates. Everyone knows the demons they fight in secret.
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” No one can examine you; you examine yourself. “Know ye not your own selves”: you know the evil you are fighting inside, the thoughts you have, the things you do in secret thinking no one sees you. Look in the mirror and ask, self, am I real? Some say they are in the faith, but in secret they are in the midst of all type of evil, giving in again and again to lasciviousness and fornication. If you cannot examine yourself, you are reprobate. Paul prayed “that ye do no evil”, and the same goes for brothers and sisters today.

Then Timothy: “Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” God knows who belongs to him. “And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” Every one of us that calls upon the name of the Lord must depart from iniquity. You brothers should not be adulterers, dealing with prostitutes, dealing with hoes. You sisters should not be sleeping around. No one should be doing schemes and credit card fraud.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” There are not just vessels of gold here in IUIC. The dishonourable one is faking it in here, here for his own reasons and ulterior motives. So ask yourself: am I real or am I fake? Which vessel are you? Only you alone know, and you have to choose which one you want to be.

Every one of us has demons and thorns we are fighting, so do not act perfect here while Satan has you in a chokehold during the week. We understand you are burning after years of doing it on the regular and now going cold turkey, but come talk to the brothers, go talk to the sisters, and ask for help. Do not let your sins weigh you down and destroy you, because God will judge.

David said examine me, and Paul says, “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” When you come into this truth you should be able to identify your own hang-ups, weaknesses and emotional problems, so when you are tested you catch yourself: this is a test, I almost fell, Satan, you almost got me. “Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” I can’t prove you; you have to prove your own self. We thought we knew some people, and found out we never really knew them.

precepts.why: Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard. You know this one: he is telling you again, examine yourselves. Go back to the beginning, Christ is saying, go back to the beginning when you heard this word. “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” So the same thing Paul said to the Corinthians, Christ said to the pastor of the church of Sardis: remember how you have received and heard, and hold fast, and repent.

points: This is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established. So Paul says, I have dealt with this matter with you on numerous occasions.

I told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them which heretofore have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare. So Paul says, if I have to come to you again about the same thing, dealing with lasciviousness, dealing with fornication, dealing with all the manner of sins that he listed, he is not going to spare.
Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness. Then he says, if I were present I would use sharpness, meaning being fierce.
According to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction. And it is not to destruction.

For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you. Because as they were learning the gospel of Christ, he is now affirming the power of God among them. He is affirming how God raised up Jesus through his power, the same way he is going to do with us.

Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. What did Paul tell them? Examine yourselves. And you have to prove your own self. We read that in Sirach earlier, about proving what is good for thy soul, proving what is good unto thy life. You have to prove these things.

So when that brother asked that question last week, it goes much deeper than just, how do I recognize or how do I deal with bitterness? We have got to start dealing with the things prior to the bitterness. Is it the person you are bitter towards? Is it because of envy? Is it because of covetousness? Is it because you rejected God altogether, meaning you do not believe? And it is not just for the brother who asked the question, it is for all of us. When that bitterness is springing up, we have to find out what are the contributing factors to the bitterness, to the hatred. Are you telling me you woke up this morning with the mindset just to hate a brother or hate a sister? And if you do have that hatred, if you do have that bitterness, what led up to it? So now you know what to fix.

For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth. So there is nothing they can do against this truth but for the truth. No matter what light they are painting us in, it is going to be for the growth of this truth.

Because by putting us on that list, you draw interest. People say, what, how can there be a group that is number three and we have never heard of it? Then naturally people are going to look into it. Some people do not take people's word at face value. They are going to research things. They are going to watch the videos to see what makes them number three most hated group. And off of that some people are going to say, she is wrong, let me watch some more videos. There is no such thing as bad publicity.

And those who are meant to be in this truth, it does not matter how they hear the truth, whether it was in a positive light or a negative light. They are going to go look at some videos and say, oh damn, they are actually speaking the truth, I need to join. Because the true prophets of the Lord, we are like Manchurian candidates. The moment we hear it, we know that is the way. Whether it was from somebody talking trash about us or somebody talking good about us.

When we are at our weakest, that is when Christ is strong within us. As times get hard, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. Paul understood that Christ is his source.

How can you be in the truth and deny the truth? How can you be in the truth and want to continue as a whoremonger, a thief, a liar, deceitful? The truth is supposed to expose those things within us so we can examine ourselves and be closer to God. No temptation that we go through is uncommon to man, but the Lord is going to give you a way to escape.

points: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Examine yourself does not mean you are in sin; it means stop and see yourself, because the one thing brothers cannot do is examine their own selves; they want to examine everybody else. Are you in the midst of watching porn? Things keep happening to you, a car accident, you lost your car, you lost your job, your wife is about to leave; why you and not everybody else? Stop and examine yourself. You are doing something you have no business doing, and then you lie to yourself and lie to us: I did not do anything.

Know ye not your own selves? Nobody here knows you more than you. Do not call me asking what I think you should change about yourself; you know you more than I know you. When a brother asks that question, he knows exactly what he should change. Maybe stop watching porn. Brothers, stop it.

Examine yourself and prove your own self: know your limitations and where your borders are before you prove with someone else, and when you hear clearly that what he wants is not you, end it instead of forcing it.
